_doc: Phất Y Cốc lineage (rules-proposals R5). Re-leaned Metal, Wind -> Metal, Fire: no place in Ngọc Hành Sơn has Wind qi, and the valley and its steppe holdings carry Fire 16-36 %. Wind stays as the founder's secret art, which only a Wind root can learn and which is outside the admission rule (as Thính Vũ keeps Thunder out of its lineage elements). Outer gate: dry-road-sword-primer (proposal, Yellow, Metal + Fire). Inner gate and above: ten-paces-sword-canon (proposal, Profound, Metal). Secret arts: debt-ledger-blade (existing, catalogue-blade; the hired sword's manual), afterimage-sword-canon (existing, catalogue-blade; elders), brushed-sleeve-step (proposal, the founder's Wind art). Unpriced.

secret.note: taught to every sword before its first contract
the founder's; Wind roots only. Thang Vô Tạ is the only living holder

lineage.tree_route_note: The hired sword's road: Edge of Autumn for the sword, Sword Spine and Sword Bow for the crit that the Tenth Pace grows into its killing cut.

techniques.name: Dry Road Sword Primer (Hạn Lộ Kiếm Quyết)
techniques.concept: The caravan guard's method, taught to the outer gate on the hot steppe roads below the valley. It draws Metal from the ore hills and Fire from the noon ground, either one, and keeps a sword arm loose through a long day's heat. It fights in short exchanges and gets stronger the longer the guard has been on the road.

arts.concept: A stance: each foe hit on you while it holds is partly turned onto your sword (less damage taken) and grants a stack of Heat that strengthens your next cut.

techniques.lore: Written by the second head Liễu Hành Vân for the companies she hired out to the camel trains of Đà Đội Thôn, so that a girl from the hot springs and a boy from the copper mines could learn the same sword.

techniques.name: Ten Paces Sword Canon (Thập Bộ Kiếm Kinh)
techniques.concept: Named for the old verse the valley lives by: ten paces, one man; a thousand li, no trace (Lý Bạch, Hiệp Khách Hành). The cultivator counts steps instead of breaths. In a fight, each second you are Moving and strike nothing stores a Pace; at ten the next strike is a killing cut that spends them all, and the holder steps back out of reach. It is a method for finishing a contract, not for winning a war.

arts.concept: Spends all stored Paces on one Metal strike whose damage and crit chance grow with each Pace; at ten Paces it ignores part of the foe's defence.
After your hit makes the foe Broken or breaks a ward, you step away: you gain evade for a moment and are At range for 1 s.

techniques.lore: The founder Quách Vô Tích's method, the canon every inner disciple of the valley takes before their first contract. The founder cut the verse into the cliff above the valley mouth, where every hired sword passes it on the way out.

techniques.name: Brushed Sleeve Step (Phất Y Bộ)
techniques.concept: The founder's own art, from the other half of the verse: when the deed is done, brush your sleeve and go. It runs on Wind alone. The holder moves on the air between one step and the next, and a sleeve brushed across a blade turns it. Taught only to a Wind root; the valley has had two in six centuries.

arts.concept: Turns the next attack aimed at the holder with a sweep of the sleeve and moves them a short distance on the wind; for a breath after, their Metal strikes are faster.
For a few seconds the holder's strikes leave afterimages that strike again a moment later; while it lasts, foes cannot single them out.

techniques.lore: Quách Vô Tích taught it to no one and left it in a sleeve of grey cloth in the valley's hall when he walked away in 790. Liễu Hành Vân, who had no Wind, kept the book closed for three centuries until a hawk-catcher's son from Thương Ưng Đài opened it: Thang Vô Tạ.
